summary: El Grande is a tense area-majority game where you're constantly recalculating who controls which region as caballeros shift each round, with the castillo and king's-region rules forcing hard tactical trade-offs. It's a slow-building, cerebral tug-of-war where the scoring rounds every third turn create real peaks of tension.
praised: Elegant, tightly interlocking rule set that still feels rich decades later
Power-card turn-order auction is a clever tension point every round
High player interaction through constant area-majority shifts
Action cards add variety and replayability without bloating the rules
Considered a classic/foundational Euro area-control design
criticised: Can feel a bit dry or abstract thematically despite the Spain setting
Slower turns and downtime, especially at higher player counts
Some find the king-movement/adjacency rule fiddly to track
Newer players can be crushed by experienced players' timing of scoring rounds

interaction.kind: area majority and blocking via troop placement

scoring.why: Points come from majority control in multiple regions at three scoring rounds plus secretive castillo bonuses, so the winner is whoever times region control best across the whole game.
